evidence.note: Early match has real swings: 'Hall snaps off superplex - Hitman takes 29 damage' drops both wrestlers to GROUNDED after a reversed hurricanrana on turn 3. This opening stretch (turns 1-30) is the only part with genuine momentum trade-offs.

'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick - Hall takes 19 damage' puts Hall at 1 HP on turn 87. The match then runs 91 more turns without resolving, so the entire back half is played out at a health total that should have been decisive.
'Hall recovers 5 stamina' restores health from 1 to 6. Recover is used 36 times total, 22 of them after turn 90, so chip damage never sticks and the match cannot converge to a finish.

Loop tax fires - 'The counter is getting predictable - Hitman slips free with momentum' - but the tie-up/counter loop simply resumes: collar_elbow on turns 99, 103, 105, 113, 119, 123, 139, 155, 169 against grapple_counter on 100, 104, 114, 120, 140, 156, 170. The tax fired only twice in the whole match (turns 104 and 124) and broke nothing.

Both wrestlers sit at 1 HP with an identical five-option menu (tie-up 91%, climb, roundhouse 86%, straight right 91%, recover) repeated verbatim from turn 115 onward. No Finish intent is offered while the opponent is standing, so there is no decision that can end the match.
The finish arrives only because the CPU lands 'razor's edge' on turn 176 and the player fails 'Fight to your feet' on 177. Player agency in the climax is a single forced one-option turn.

State feedback is clear where it exists: 'Hall is yanked up - their legs aren't under them yet!' correctly narrates pending_groggy applied on pickup, and turn 88 'Escape momentum builds for Hall' explains the failed-rise reward.

Bare reversal log 'Hitman turns the tables!' names no move and no actor intent. The player chose Collar-and-elbow tie-up on turn 105 and read only 'Hall turns the tables!' - it is impossible to tell from the log whether the tie-up was attempted, blocked, or reversed.

'Hall recovers 5 stamina' increases the transcript health field from 1 to 6. Labeling a health restore as stamina is misleading; a new player watching HP tick back up has no vocabulary that matches the log line.

Curation is honest about pin: 'Finish | Cover - pinfall attempt | pin' is shown whenever the opponent is grounded (turns 41, 47, 61, 81, 89). But that is only 5 of 89 player turns, and from turn 91 onward the Finish intent never reappears despite Hall sitting at 1-11 HP, with no menu text explaining that a finish requires grounding first.
Percentage semantics read correctly: 'Finish | Sharpshooter | 86%' with note 'cash in momentum for a match-ending swing' sits next to the unlabeled 'pin', so the 86% is not presented as a win chance.

stickiness.rematch_reason: The first 30 turns were genuinely varied (top-rope exchanges, superplex, collision course, grapple counters), but the 90-turn attrition stalemate at 1-11 HP is a strong deterrent. I would only queue another match to see whether a different policy avoids the no-finish deadlock, not because this match created curiosity.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 228 with the methodical policy and take the offered 'Finish | Cover - pinfall attempt' on turn 89 (Hall grounded at 1 HP) instead of 'Pull opponent up', to confirm the deadlock is a policy artifact rather than a missing standing-finish path.

evidence.note: Discovery moments exist early: 'Hitman snaps off top-rope brawl shot - Hall takes 11 damage' during a rare TOP_ROPE vs TOP_ROPE exchange, supported by position_diversity 12.
'The crowd gasps - Hall is busted open; blood streams down their face' is the kind of one-off surprise that drives rematch curiosity, but it changed nothing and the match continued for 57 more turns.
Turns 149-153 repeat roundhouse kick / recover / shake the cobwebs with logs already seen dozens of times; log_uniqueness_ratio 0.3819 means roughly three in five lines were reruns.

The finisher beat lands well: 'Hall snaps off razor's edge - Hitman takes 20 damage' plus '- FINISHER - the next cover packs extra heat', and turn 178 pays it off with 'The finisher still echoes - +12 on the cover!' followed by a stepped referee count (delays 0.0/1.0/1.5).

The blood spot 'The crowd gasps - Hall is busted open; blood streams down their face' produced no state shift - health, momentum, and position are unchanged apart from the 9 damage - so the biggest narrative line in the match carries no mechanical weight.
near_fall_count is 0 across 178 turns; the only pin attempt in the match is the one that ends it, so there is never a kickout or two-count to build tension.
'Hall recovers 5 stamina' appears 36 times and 'Hitman tries to rise but can't find it' style lines 22 times; the dominant texture of the match is repeated low-stakes filler rather than payoff beats.

top_issues.summary: No way to close out a standing, nearly dead opponent. From turn 91 to 178 Hall never drops below 1 HP and never rises above 11, but the curated menu offers Finish/pin only while the opponent is GROUNDED (5 of 89 player turns). The match ran 178 turns and failed the [8, 40] pacing gate as a direct result.

Loop persists despite the loop tax. The tie-up/counter loop ran nine iterations (collar_elbow on turns 99, 103, 105, 113, 119, 123, 139, 155, 169) and the anti-loop feedback fired only twice, on turn 104 ('The counter is getting predictable') and turn 124 ('Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum'). Neither instance changed the pattern.

Recover out-paces chip damage at low health. 'Catch your breath' fired 22 times after turn 90, restoring 5 health each time against 5-9 damage strikes, producing a ~90-turn attrition stalemate with zero near-falls.
'Catch your breath' logs 'recovers 5 stamina' but raises the health value (turn 92: 1 -> 6). The word in the log does not match the stat that moves.
Bare reversal lines like 'Hitman turns the tables!' (turn 84) and 'Hall turns the tables!' (turn 105) omit the attempted move, so the player cannot tell what failed.
top_issues.suggested_area: action log phrasing for reversed setup moves
